title: Open with the decision, then reduce uncertainty
summary: A strong opening restates the objective and asks only the questions that can materially change the structure or recommendation.
principles: Restate the metric, change, time period, and decision before investigating.
Ask about definitions, scope, timing, and real decision constraints.
Avoid long question lists and details that cannot change the first structure.
example: For a margin decline, confirm the metric and timing, then clarify constraints on pricing, investment, and customer experience.
